approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves fresh molecular graphs from the current session’s accepted population and chooses evaluations with correlated function draws from a count-fingerprint Gaussian process. It fits a monotone unit-linear transformation of accepted scores, then maps the latent predictions back to score units. Its active draws use the original raw-GP mean while retaining the warped law’s centered residuals. A separate, fixed-amplitude warped expectation ranks the forty eligible candidates when progress stalls. This complete location host improved its own endpoint panel, even though prediction loss and interval coverage worsened.
approach.novelty: Learn one signal variance jointly with the existing nine warp coefficients and use the resulting centered inverse law around the same raw-GP location. Independently retain the Parent’s fixed-amplitude warp for eligibility. The new degree can change conditional spread, shape and dependence without changing those location and gate consumers. An earlier signal fit changed these consumers together and lacked two successful endpoints; the present test uses the complete location host and preserves the earlier result’s limits. The separate amplitude sibling holds every fit fixed, so it answers a different question.

finding_summary.headline: Signal-centered laws improve paid prediction but lose endpoint score on the complete location host.
finding_summary.insights: The exposed covariance intervention does not deliver its registered endpoint benefit on this host. Lack of fitting, feedback or purchase exposure is not the explanation. Same-paid pinball loss improves from 0.020657 to 0.018415 and 90% coverage rises from 68.0% to 77.7%, yet three cells lose on pinball and six lose coverage. Active, fixed-translated and raw-GP means have identical MSE and ordering by construction, so the predictive improvement does not establish improved mean ranking. Positive gain over actual generating parents rises from 14.04774 to 14.46471 overall and from 3.45342 to 5.26428 late, while total incumbent progress falls from 5.53536 to 5.09506 despite a late increase. Local gains and predictive quality therefore do not establish useful adaptive allocation or causal mediation. A model or acquisition rule that measures improvement utility could address this conversion gap, but its benefit is untested here. The molecular audit separately shows more heavy growth:983 accepted outputs exceed 40 heavy atoms versus 116 for the Parent, with 104 versus 70 very small fragments; no stereochemistry is specified despite 2,394 outputs with potential unassigned centres. More formal scaffold identities coexist with concentrated high-scoring families. Task-agnostic graph proposals that explicitly handle growth, contraction, ring topology and stereochemical choices address those measured coverage limitations; the observations establish neither a universal filter nor a chemical cause of the score loss. The reused likelihood derivative and inverse-moment operations worked under their registered restricted adaptation;382 of 435 joint fits used function-reduction termination, so this is evidence about the finite numerical recipe, not globally optimal fitting. The donor’s incomplete result and all earlier verdicts remain intact, and broader approach usefulness and retained-component contributions remain open.
finding_summary.results: All 435 joint fits,435 independent fixed-law fits and 4,350 original five-law predictions completed, with all 15 tasks exiting successfully. The preserved location and gate passed source, saved-state and runtime checks. Signal fitting changed 398 purchase sets and introduced 1,472 actual-only purchases;1,402 met the strict price-reversal exposure condition. Every nonterminal purchase reached the next fit, while 150 final-batch purchases remain correctly censored. The endpoint macro fell from 0.577516 to 0.548163, a paired loss of 0.029353 against the required gain of 0.002. All three seed macros fell;13 task/seed endpoints worsened and two improved. Sitagliptin accounts for 79.8% of the net loss. The separate formal-Anchor deficit is 0.058867, and the literal formal goal remains inapplicable because this experiment has a different code Parent. The original request does not supply this Child’s paired task-safety threshold or result.

molecular.overall_character: This describes n-85ae5a42a8bb against its exact code Parent n-d17e2a492177 under the original issued Search panel. All fifteen Child and fifteen Parent trajectories were read in full, together with six summaries and thirty individual task-result files. Each cell contains 300 accepted records: ten initial and 290 optimizer observations. Thus each node contributes 4,350 optimizer records and 150 initial records; all 9,000 structures parse with RDKit 2023.09.6. The summaries and individual task files agree with trajectory counts and existing score maxima. The initial SMILES and scores match in each Child/Parent cell. The original request states child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0/1/2, no profile mismatch and no tasks without trajectories. No required chemical record or summary is missing. Chemical-record completeness and supplied endpoint pairing remain separate facts; neither supplies a mechanism, eligibility or selection judgment. Among Child optimizer records, 4,231/4,350 contain rings and 4,135/4,350 contain aromatic atoms, compared with Parent 4,276 and 4,253. Aryl/heteroaryl assemblies, carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles, amine-bearing rings and extended fused or bridged graphs are present. Median heavy-atom count is 30 versus 28; p95 is 64 versus 38; the maximum is 113 versus 96. Counts above 40/50/60 heavy atoms are 983/736/301 versus 116/40/13. The large tail is concentrated: the extended aromatic/carbonyl population contributes 749 records above 40 and the amine/aryl population contributes 208. At the other tail, 104 versus 70 optimizer records have at most five heavy atoms. Molecular weight exceeds 500 in 1,311 versus 524 records. This panel therefore shows both expansion and fragmentation; it does not establish a preferred size or a size filter. No optimizer record in either node has a charged atom, specified atom chiral tag or specified E/Z/cis/trans bond stereo. There are 2,394 Child and 2,247 Parent records with at least one potential unassigned RDKit chiral centre. Neutral graph representations do not establish solution protonation, and the generator demonstrably produces nonamide aliphatic nitrogen-containing structures. N-halogen connectivity occurs in 583 versus 654 records; O-halogen connectivity in 204 versus 348; N-O single bonds in 440 versus 330. Their distributions differ across tasks and score-selected subsets. These are explicit connectivity flags, not measured instability or biological effects. Complex closures, heteroatom-halogen links and some peroxide-bearing examples make synthetic plausibility questionable without route evidence; parsing and high recorded values do not establish synthesis, binding or developability. Definitions exactly preserve the accepted Parent report and audit: the unit is an accepted record occurrence, repeated identities across seeds remain, and initial records are separate. High and low subsets are the highest and lowest thirty optimizer records per cell and pooled per task; ordering uses recorded score descending/ascending followed by ascending seed and evaluation, without tie expansion. They are retrospective descriptive subsets, not independent replicates. Size tails are <=5 and >40/>50/>60 heavy atoms. Typed Murcko and MakeScaffoldGeneric scaffolds use canonical isomeric strings, excluding empty scaffolds and recording their denominators. Similarity uses binary radius-2, 2,048-bit Morgan fingerprints with includeChirality=True and every unordered within-task record pair after excluding fewer than ten heavy atoms. Cross-seed repeated identities remain; there is no cross-task similarity, and pooled pair means are not averages of seed means. This fingerprint is distinct from the optimizer count kernel. The inherited carbonyl SMARTS includes aliphatic C=O and aromatic c=O; the nonamide aliphatic-nitrogen SMARTS is a graph pattern, not a pKa test. Counts are record-presence counts, not atom totals. All Parent per-cell and pooled initial/optimizer/high30/low30 descriptors and denominators, plus global totals, reproduce the accepted historical audit exactly. There are no definition differences. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
